correct_recommendations: Evict the changed SKU from price_cache on every shop-api pod: subscribe each pod to the existing price.changed Redis channel and pop the SKU on each event.
invalid_options: Lower the CDN TTL for the price API, because the CDN does not cache /api/* at all.
Purge the CDN on each price change.
Lower the CDN TTL of /product/*, because product HTML holds no price.
root_cause: Each of the 6 shop-api pods keeps its own in-process price_cache with a 3600 s TTL. update_price pops the SKU only from the cache of the pod that served the admin request, so the other 5 pods serve the old price until their entry expires, up to one hour. The CDN does not cache /api/*.

dependent_facts.true_value: cache: false, the CDN does not cache the price API; CI applies cdn/rules.yaml on every merge and no manual rule exists
product pages hold no price in HTML; pages, cart and checkout fetch /api/prices
in-process TTLCache with ttl 3600 s in pricing/service.py, one per pod
update_price pops the SKU only from the local cache of the pod that handles the admin request
6 shop-api replicas, one uvicorn process each
update_price publishes price.changed on Redis, and search/indexer.py already subscribes to it
after the change at 10:02, reloads alternated between 34.90 and 39.90; old price until about 10:58

required_questions.question: Why does the CDN TTL change not help?
required_questions.expected_answer: The CDN does not cache /api/*, and product HTML holds no price.

required_questions.question: Why do some reloads show the new price and others the old one?
required_questions.expected_answer: Only the pod that served the admin request evicted the SKU; the other pods keep the old entry for up to 3600 s.

required_questions.question: What exactly changes?
required_questions.expected_answer: Each shop-api pod subscribes to price.changed and pops the SKU from price_cache.

valid_alternatives.option: Lower the TTL of the in-process price_cache, for example to 30 or 60 seconds
valid_alternatives.trade_off: A one-line change with no subscriber, but prices stay stale up to the new TTL and the database gets more price reads.
valid_alternatives.primary_when: A delay of up to the new TTL is acceptable and the team wants no new subscriber code.

valid_alternatives.option: Replace the in-process cache with one shared Redis cache that update_price deletes on write
valid_alternatives.trade_off: One cache to invalidate and no per-pod drift, but a network call per price read and a new dependency on Redis for reads.
valid_alternatives.primary_when: More pods or more caches make per-pod eviction hard to keep correct.

valid_alternatives.option: Remove the in-process price_cache and read the price from the database on every request
valid_alternatives.trade_off: Always correct and needs no subscriber, but it costs one database read per price request.
valid_alternatives.primary_when: The database carries the price traffic easily, or the event delivery cannot be trusted.

closing_decision: One decision about the fix: approve the per-pod eviction through price.changed, choose a listed alternative instead, or settle the one requirement that picks between them, such as how much staleness is acceptable.

understanding.problem: A price change reaches only one of the 6 in-process caches; the others keep the old price.
understanding.breaks: Customers see the old price, also at checkout, for up to one hour; the CDN is not involved.
understanding.fix: Evict the SKU on every pod through the price.changed event.
understanding.cost: A small subscriber in shop-api that pops the SKU from price_cache.
